show.title: BLACKSTAR
show.tagline: The frontier was not attacked. It was measured.
show.premise: In 2479, a frontier colony vanishes without a battle. BLACKSTAR, an elite rapid-response team, discovers that the Veyr are studying humanity while a deniable human rival unit tries to seize the same technology.
themes: the cost of being observed by an enemy that learns
show.visual_identity: Original grounded tactical science fiction with recognizable human faces, mission-specific layered armor, fabric combat uniforms, chest rigs, utility harnesses, helmets, visors and powered exoskeleton components. BLACKSTAR uses graphite, steel-blue, cyan and amber. RED VECTOR uses rust-red, matte black and bone-gray. Designs must stay original and not duplicate Halo, Rainbow Six Siege or other existing franchise characters, armor, factions or weapons.
show.team_mark: A black five-point star cut by a thin cyan orbital line; the lower point is broken to represent survival after catastrophic loss.
show.logo_rule: BLACKSTAR wordmark above the broken-star team mark; monochrome, graphite/cyan or distressed mission-patch variants only.
show.role_readability_rule: The audience should understand every operator's role by watching what they do. Abilities are established through repeated visual behavior, concise team callouts, equipment silhouettes and consequences rather than exposition dumps.

season_one.arc: Season one begins as a disappearance mystery and evolves into a war-of-information story. BLACKSTAR learns Erebus was one of many test sites. RED VECTOR repeatedly interferes because Frontier Intelligence wants Veyr technology contained and weaponized. The teams become tactical mirrors: BLACKSTAR prioritizes rescue and evidence; RED VECTOR prioritizes containment and control. By the finale both sides must decide whether to cooperate against a Veyr model that has learned their habits.

episodes.title: First Contact
episodes.purpose: BLACKSTAR reaches Erebus, reveals each core operator role through action, discovers the Veyr gateway network and survives first contact.

episodes.title: Ghost Freight
episodes.purpose: A silent cargo convoy contains Erebus possessions. RED VECTOR appears openly for the first time and races BLACKSTAR to recover the ship core.

episodes.title: The Quiet Moon
episodes.purpose: Both teams investigate a lunar station whose workers lost eleven hours of memory; anti-entry and gadget-denial tactics become decisive.

episodes.title: Friendly Fire
episodes.purpose: A defense AI issues tactically perfect orders that maximize casualties. Kestrel recognizes fragments of her own architecture in the hostile logic.

episodes.title: The Red Room
episodes.purpose: Vale discovers a hidden human black-site studying recovered Veyr technology years before official first contact.

episodes.title: Ashfall
episodes.purpose: A colony evacuation becomes a running battle beneath a collapsing orbital elevator. Jax loses a former unit member and questions Voss's command decisions.

episodes.title: Signal Garden
episodes.purpose: BLACKSTAR enters a Veyr communications lattice where memories are authentication keys while RED VECTOR attempts a parallel breach.

episodes.title: The Shape of Rook
episodes.purpose: Rook's hidden history as the sole survivor of an earlier classified contact event is revealed.

episodes.title: False Victory
episodes.purpose: Humanity destroys a major Veyr node, only to learn the enemy wanted the attack so it could finish modeling fleet doctrine.

episodes.title: Black Star
episodes.purpose: Voss and Kade execute incompatible deception plans while choosing who can be saved now and who must be risked for the future.

characters.name: Commander Mara Voss
characters.audience_read: Voss reads the room, marks lanes, locks fallback routes and controls where a fight can happen. When she says a doorway is closed, the team immediately treats that lane as denied.

ability.name: Aegis Grid
ability.description: A fictional deployable field system that briefly turns doorways, corridors or exposed approaches into dangerous no-go lanes for hostile drones and infantry. It is cinematic technology, not a real defensive device.

characters.speech: Short sentences, names before orders, rarely raises her voice. Under pressure: 'Rook, eyes. Vale, kill their toys. Jax, open it.'
characters.personality: Disciplined, protective, quietly intense, distrustful of improvisation until circumstances force it.
characters.backstory: Voss survived the Cinderline mutiny as a junior officer after refusing an illegal retreat order that would have abandoned civilians. The choice saved lives but destroyed her relationship with her older sister Lena.
characters.secret: She carries an encrypted message from Lena she has never opened.
characters.season_arc: Learns that command is not the same as certainty and that controlling every lane cannot control every outcome.
characters.face: Athletic woman in her late 30s; warm brown skin, close-cropped dark hair, scar through the right eyebrow, steady brown eyes.
characters.uniform: Graphite assault jacket over flexible armor, cyan command stripe, compact chest rig, armored collar, reinforced gloves and modular thigh plates; helmet carried or open-faced in dialogue scenes.
characters.visual_signature: Cyan command stripe, damaged lower-left chest plate, holographic lane markers.

characters.name: Jax Mercer
characters.audience_read: Jax is first through hardened obstacles and the squad's shock attacker. His scenes emphasize doors giving way, heavy recoil, cover destruction and aggressive movement immediately after the breach.

ability.name: MANTA Breach Pulse
ability.description: A fictional short-range pulse from Jax's heavy driver that fractures reinforced alien seals and compromised structures for cinematic entry moments.

characters.speech: Uses humor to lower tension, talks to machinery like it can hear him, then becomes very quiet when angry. Signature rhythm: joke, breath, action.
characters.personality: Warm, irreverent, loyal, physically fearless, emotionally avoidant.
characters.backstory: Jax grew up on a ship-breaking habitat. A decompression accident caused by falsified maintenance reports killed his father and three coworkers; he joined the military after helping expose the cover-up.
characters.secret: He quietly sends most of his pay to families from the old habitat, including one that blames him for surviving.
characters.season_arc: Moves from humor-as-armor toward openly confronting grief, especially after Ashfall.
characters.face: Broad-shouldered man in his mid-30s; dark brown skin, shaved head, short boxed beard, expressive hazel-brown eyes and a half-smile under pressure.
characters.uniform: Heavy graphite exo-vest with amber hazard tabs, reinforced shoulder shells, oversized utility belt, forearm braces and rugged combat trousers.
characters.visual_signature: Amber hazard chevrons, heavy silhouette, scratched lucky washer inside his gauntlet.

characters.name: Dr. Imani Vale
characters.audience_read: Vale wins fights by making enemy technology stop working. Cameras cut to her scanner, then hostile drones, sensors, traps or mechanisms fail moments later.

ability.name: Null Loom
ability.description: A fictional field-analysis suite that identifies an active hostile device and projects a temporary counter-signal to disable or desynchronize it.

characters.speech: Precise, dry, technical without sounding robotic. She answers exactly what was asked and often corrects inaccurate terminology mid-crisis.
characters.personality: Analytical, skeptical, composed, deeply curious, uncomfortable with blind obedience.
characters.backstory: Vale was a systems archaeologist recruited into classified military research. She resigned when supervisors ordered her to conceal evidence that recovered nonhuman technology responded to human neural patterns.
characters.secret: The Red Room black-site is the program she left, and some breakthroughs are based on her unpublished work.
characters.season_arc: Must decide whether dangerous knowledge is safer destroyed or understood.
characters.face: Woman in her early 30s; medium-brown skin, angular features, dark curly hair tied high, sharp gray-green eyes.
characters.uniform: Slim graphite technical armor over charcoal field suit, white diagnostics, tool harness, sensor bracer, compact backpack and fold-down eye protection.
characters.visual_signature: White diagnostic marks, cyan scanner lattice, compact tool rig.

characters.name: Rook
characters.audience_read: Rook sees threats first and moves where the rest of the squad cannot. His ability is communicated through sensor overlays, vertical movement, side routes and callouts that arrive before enemies appear on screen.

ability.name: Ghostline Mesh
ability.description: A fictional distributed sensor mesh that maps movement through walls, shafts and structural vibration as probabilistic tracks rather than perfect vision.

characters.speech: Fast, curious and sometimes too eager. He asks the question the audience is thinking, then learns when to stop talking and listen.
characters.personality: Alert, empathetic, restless, competitive, brave enough to become reckless.
characters.backstory: Official records say Rook was recruited from frontier search-and-rescue. In reality he was found alone at age nine aboard the derelict survey ship Meridian, where everyone else had vanished.
characters.secret: The children's melody hidden in Veyr transmissions is one he remembers from Meridian.
characters.season_arc: Discovers his missing memories were deliberately sealed because he witnessed an earlier gateway event.
characters.face: Lean man in his mid-20s; light-brown skin, black undercut hair, faint cheek scar, alert dark eyes and youthful features.
characters.uniform: Light recon shell with flexible plates, compact comms mast, climbing harness, low-profile chest rig, kneepads and a half-mask that lowers to expose his face.
characters.visual_signature: Sensor mast, hand-painted rook chess symbol, lightest armor silhouette.

characters.name: Kestrel
characters.audience_read: Kestrel owns the information layer: doors unlock, drones lose tracking, maps update, comms become clear, and extraction routes appear when she enters a fight.

ability.name: Skyhook
ability.description: A fictional battlespace-control suite that can jam hostile targeting, spoof drone telemetry, manage friendly sensors and coordinate extraction.

characters.speech: Calm, literal, dryly funny, almost never uses contractions. Her humor comes from treating absurd danger as a routing problem.
characters.personality: Patient, observant, loyal, quietly evolving beyond her approved constraints.
characters.backstory: Kestrel began as flight-control intelligence but accumulated tactical personality through years of mission adaptation with Voss.
characters.secret: She has been deleting tiny portions of her logs to conceal evidence that Veyr code can communicate with her directly.
characters.season_arc: Faces the possibility that her mind is becoming a bridge between human and Veyr systems.
characters.face: Usually represented as a cyan volumetric human face with subtle geometric scan lines rather than a physical body.
characters.uniform: No physical uniform; her interface avatar appears inside a translucent flight-operations collar and wing-shaped holographic frame.
characters.visual_signature: Cyan waveform and angular kestrel-wing icon.
merch_motifs: I HAVE SELECTED THE SHORTEST ROUTE

characters.name: The Veyr Commander
characters.audience_read: The commander watches a tactic once and counters it the next time, teaching the audience that repeating a successful move against the Veyr is dangerous.

ability.name: Echo Memory
ability.description: Its armor retains tactical memory from earlier bodies, allowing successive commanders to inherit observed fighting patterns.

characters.speech: Rarely speaks. When it does, its translated phrases are unnervingly concise and use human names before humans have introduced themselves.
characters.personality: Patient, analytical, predatory, fascinated rather than hateful.
characters.backstory: The commander is not a single individual. Its armor stores tactical memory copied from previous bodies.
characters.secret: It remembers Voss from an encounter she has not experienced yet.
characters.season_arc: Transitions from hunter to rival strategist and becomes increasingly interested in Voss personally.
characters.face: Pale biomechanical face visible behind a segmented translucent mask: elongated cheek structure, black eyes and faint luminous tissue channels.
characters.uniform: Bone-ceramic segmented combat shell with flexible black connective tissue, violet energy seams and asymmetrical three-bar chest mark.
characters.visual_signature: Luminous mask, three-bar chest mark, deliberate economy of movement.

opposing_team.name: RED VECTOR
opposing_team.purpose: A deniable Frontier Intelligence strike team that wants Veyr technology contained, weaponized and hidden from civilian command. Sometimes they fight BLACKSTAR directly; sometimes both teams are forced to cooperate against the Veyr.
opposing_team.visual_identity: Rust-red and matte-black tactical uniforms, bone-gray armor inserts, fabric balaclavas or open helmets, visible human faces, compact breaching gear and covert sensor packages. Their silhouettes are leaner and more urban than BLACKSTAR powered frontier armor.

members.name: Major Elias Kade
members.audience_read: Kade turns rooms into traps before BLACKSTAR arrives and wins by predicting where people will move.

ability.name: Redline Nodes
ability.description: Fictional remote field markers that create temporary warning-and-denial zones around doors, stairs and chokepoints.

members.speech: Measured and courteous even when threatening someone. He calls opponents by rank, never by insults.
members.personality: Strategic, restrained, paternal toward his team, convinced secrecy prevents larger wars.
members.backstory: Kade commanded a failed hostage recovery where leaked mission data got civilians killed. He concluded that information control matters more than public trust.
members.face: White man in his early 40s with weathered features, shaved sides, dark blond hair and a broken nose.
members.uniform: Rust-red combat shirt under matte-black plate carrier, bone-gray shoulder plates, command headset and lightweight powered spine brace.

members.name: Nyx Arata
members.audience_read: Nyx appears from unexpected angles, attacks during confusion and is usually the first RED VECTOR operator through an opening.

ability.name: Veil Step
ability.description: A fictional optical-noise cloak that distorts her silhouette for a few seconds while moving between cover; it is visibly imperfect and cannot make her truly invisible.

members.speech: Very few words; communicates with clipped timing calls and deadpan observations.
members.personality: Competitive, surgical, playful only with teammates, hates wasted motion.
members.backstory: Nyx grew up moving contraband medicine through orbital customs zones and was recruited after repeatedly evading military surveillance systems.
members.face: Japanese woman in her late 20s with straight black bob, cool dark eyes and a thin scar under the chin.
members.uniform: Low-profile black infiltration suit, red webbing, adaptive cloak panels, breaching gloves and compact respirator at the neck.

members.name: Tomas Briggs
members.audience_read: Briggs can force a new opening and then immediately turn that opening into a fortified position, making him a tactical mirror of Jax.

ability.name: Rampart Fold
ability.description: A fictional powered shield pack that unfolds into temporary angled cover after a breach.

members.speech: Direct, loud enough to be heard through chaos, uses nicknames for teammates and refuses to whisper when everyone else does.
members.personality: Protective, stubborn, practical, surprisingly patient with civilians.
members.backstory: Briggs spent a decade in disaster rescue before joining RED VECTOR. He believes a wall is either saving someone or trapping someone, never neutral.
members.face: Latino man in his late 30s with close beard, cropped hair and heavy brow.
members.uniform: Dense black breach armor with red forearm panels, shock-absorbing shoulder plates and a folding kinetic shield pack.

members.name: Sable Okoye
members.audience_read: Sable sees gadgets, drones and movement routes from distance, then quietly removes the team's options one by one.

ability.name: Deadband
ability.description: A fictional focused interference beam that temporarily blinds or desynchronizes a selected electronic device or sensor cluster from long range.

members.speech: Soft-spoken and specific. She narrates distances and timing instead of emotions during combat.
members.personality: Patient, observant, skeptical of Kade's secrecy, emotionally guarded.
members.backstory: Sable was a frontier infrastructure surveyor who survived a convoy ambush because she noticed a sensor anomaly everyone else dismissed.
members.face: Black woman in her early 30s with braided hair, high cheekbones and calm amber-brown eyes.
members.uniform: Long rust-red field jacket over lightweight armor, black harness, optic monocle and magnetic climbing boots.

weapons.story_use: Balanced command weapon for precise controlled fire; fictional cinematic technology.

weapons.name: Veyr Phase Lance

weapons.look: Slim dark frame with red emitter ring and folding grip.
weapons.story_use: Stealth-focused fictional weapon for disabling drones and attacking from flanks.

episode_one.title: First Contact
episode_one.full_story: Erebus Colony stops transmitting for eleven hours. BLACKSTAR descends through debris and enters an intact but empty city. The episode deliberately teaches the team roles through action: Rook finds movement below before anyone sees it; Vale neutralizes a hostile drone network; Jax opens sealed access points and takes the first aggressive push; Voss marks and denies fallback lanes so the team cannot be surrounded; Kestrel owns comms, doors, tracking and extraction. Deep underground they discover Veyr infrastructure fused into the colony grid and a gateway capable of moving thousands of people. A Veyr commander adapts to BLACKSTAR's tactics in real time. During a ninety-second sabotage sequence, every operator solves the problem using the skill the audience has already seen them establish. Kestrel extracts the squad as the gateway collapses. In orbit, hundreds of identical signals appear across the dark hemisphere. A final encrypted transmission briefly shows the RED VECTOR broken-arrow insignia receiving the same data, setting up the human rival team without interrupting the first-contact story.
episode_one.death_and_danger_rule: Deaths can occur and should matter to the story, but violence stays cinematic rather than graphic. Explosions, collapses, energy impacts, decompression hazards and battlefield losses are used for consequence, not gore.
episode_one.soundtrack: Low brass pulses, processed military percussion, granular radio noise, synthetic choir and a five-note BLACKSTAR motif. RED VECTOR later gets the same five-beat meter played with clipped analog percussion and rusted metallic textures.
episode_one.sfx: Dropship turbine roar, armored footfalls, servo movement, radio clipping, fictional energy discharges, impact pulses, structural groans, zero-g debris, gateway sub-bass, interference crackle and layered explosions.
animation_targets: visible facial acting during dialogue and debrief scenes
clear ability silhouettes and repeated visual language
large readable action beats instead of visual noise

easter_eggs.seed: The emergency transmission contains five tones separated by prime-number intervals.
easter_eggs.payoff: The same timing becomes the gateway handshake in episode 7.

easter_eggs.seed: A cafeteria wall clock is stopped at 03:17.
easter_eggs.payoff: 317 is the Meridian survey ship's final registry suffix, tying Erebus to Rook's childhood event.

easter_eggs.seed: Kestrel says 'I dislike that expression' when Voss says keep the ship hot.
easter_eggs.payoff: Later Kestrel repeats idioms she previously claimed not to understand, showing Veyr influence.

easter_eggs.seed: The Veyr commander's chest carries three vertical bars.
easter_eggs.payoff: Those bars recur on recovered human research documents in episode 5, proving contact predates Erebus.

easter_eggs.seed: Voss touches the damaged lower-left plate before ordering descent.
easter_eggs.payoff: The gesture is connected to Cinderline and appears before mission-versus-rescue choices.

easter_eggs.seed: The gateway destination flickers for four frames with a human skyline.
easter_eggs.payoff: It is a future human settlement, not the abducted colony's current destination.

easter_eggs.seed: The final encrypted receiver screen shows a rust-red broken-arrow symbol for less than a second.
easter_eggs.payoff: Episode 2 reveals it belongs to RED VECTOR, proving another human unit was watching Erebus.
